geo.label: Fed lift-off meets war risk
parts: Macro Stance

The US goes into a holiday-shortened week with two shocks stacked on top of each other: a Fed about to start hiking into the hottest inflation in four decades, and a Russia–Ukraine standoff that Washington now describes in near-certain terms. Reuters reported US consumer prices posting their largest annual gain in 40 years as inflation became widespread [[n1968]], and Al Jazeera reported the Fed is prepared to move faster if that persists [[n1291]]. The S&P 500 closed at 4,348.87 index points, -0.72% on the session and -1.58% over five sessions, while the VIX held at 27.75 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). We are Bearish: activity is firm, but policy and geopolitics both skew against equity multiples.
Rates & Curve

The Treasury par curve remains positively sloped, but the 20-observation move is a clean bear flattening: the 2Y rose 46 bps to 1.47% from 1.01%, the 10Y only 17 bps to 1.92% from 1.75%, and the 10Y-2Y spread compressed 29 bps to +45 bps (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-18). The last five observations carry the geopolitical signal — the 2Y slipped 3 bps and the 10Y was unchanged as haven demand capped the sell-off. Reuters described the flattening as the curve pricing Fed tightening alongside fears of a policy error [[n2060]], and Eurodollar futures are already betting a hawkish Fed could ease slightly in 2024 [[n1272]]. With 10Y-3M still +157 bps, the front end is doing the tightening while the long end questions how long the cycle can run. The DXY at 96.04 index points, +0.25% on the session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18), shows the dollar absorbing risk aversion rather than reversing.
New / Most Important

The weekend raised the invasion probability decisively. The BBC reported Biden saying he is convinced Putin has decided to invade [[n1424]], the Guardian reported US warnings that Russia has amassed up to 190,000 troops on Ukraine's borders [[n1415]], and Reuters said Putin would oversee nuclear drills [[n1422]]. Fed messaging is split: Bullard again called for a front-loaded campaign, per the WSJ [[n1298]], while the New York Fed president saw no need for a big March move, according to China Daily [[n2080]]. Reuters reported the Fed is set to raise rates 25 bps in March as calls for 50 bps grow louder [[n1282]]. With US cash markets shut for Presidents' Day, the weekend's news is first repriced at home on Tuesday.
Playbook ✓

Action: stay underweight long-duration growth against pricing-power staples and energy, and carry a gold hedge. Trigger to add risk: concrete progress toward a Biden–Putin summit while the S&P 500 recovers its 20-session reference of 4,397.94 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). Trigger to press the hedge: a Tuesday open below the 4,348.87 close with the VIX above 27.75. What changes the call: credible de-escalation plus a Fed that leans toward 25 bps would let the curve steepen from +45 bps and relieve multiples; an invasion would make the 10Y's haven bid, rather than the 2Y's hike pricing, the dominant rates driver.

geo.label: Gradual ECB, gas-exposed equities
parts: Macro Stance

Europe carries the most direct exposure to a Russian move — through gas, banks and sentiment — while its central bank remains the slowest to react. The STOXX 600 closed at 460.81 index points, -1.87% over five sessions, and the DAX fell -2.48% over the same span to 15,042.51 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). Reuters flagged that European stocks are at risk if Russia invades Ukraine [[n0862]]. We stay Bearish until the gas and sanctions tail narrows.
Activity & Inflation

Inflation keeps surprising: Bankier.pl noted European inflation had again surprised economists [[n1541]], and Reuters reported UK inflation climbing to 5.5%, the highest since 1992 [[n1257]]. Yet Lagarde repeated her pledge for a gradual policy shift [[n1212]], and Reuters said the ECB would raise its deposit rate only to -0.25% by year-end [[n1211]]. Activity is resilient rather than weak: Reuters reported French unemployment at a 13-year low [[n2007]], and DW reported Germany planning to end COVID restrictions [[n1246]]. The squeeze is on real incomes — the BBC reported UK wage growth lagging the cost of living [[n1237]].
New / Most Important

Gas is the transmission line. Reuters reported European storage survived the winter but summer refilling looms [[n1273]], and Dutch TTF gas has eased to 73.76 EUR/MWh, -4.73% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18) — the market is pricing supply continuity, not disruption. Reuters' review of Europe's options in a Russian gas disruption [[n1239]] frames exactly the scenario that price does not yet reflect.
Playbook ✓

Action: underweight euro-area equities, especially Russia-sensitive banks, against the US. Trigger to cover: diplomatic progress plus TTF holding below 73.76 EUR/MWh. What changes the call: a pipeline interruption would push gas higher and turn the ECB's gradualism from a support into a stagflation problem, while a durable de-escalation would favour the cheaper European cyclicals first.

geo.label: Onshore easing, offshore squeeze
parts: Macro Stance

China is running the opposite cycle to the US — easing into a slowdown while Washington tightens into inflation — and its equity market is splitting accordingly. The Shanghai Composite closed at 3,490.76 index points, +0.66% on the session and +0.80% over five sessions, while the Hang Seng fell -1.88% to 24,327.71 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). The difference is regulation: onshore investors trade the policy put, offshore investors trade platform risk. BNP Paribas Asset Management's analysis of US–China monetary policy divergence [[n1312]] sets the macro frame, and Reuters' report that the yuan slipped under that divergence [[n0214]] shows the currency beginning to share the adjustment. Mixed: constructive on A-shares, cautious on internet platforms.
PMIs & Activity

Momentum entered the year soft. Reuters reported January factory activity contracting on the Caixin PMI as COVID lockdowns bit [[n0174]], after Global Times reported 2021 growth of 8.1%, the fastest in a decade [[n0158]]. Fixed-asset investment rose 4.9% in 2021, per Macau Business [[n0160]], and China Daily reported industrial profits rebounding on production [[n0172]] — a supply-side recovery handing over to softer domestic demand. Reuters said slowing inflation leaves room for policy easing [[n0205]]. Omicron is the swing factor: Reuters reported Hong Kong 'overwhelmed' as infections hit a record [[n0191]], and Al Jazeera reported Xi telling Hong Kong to control the outbreak [[n0238]]. The next official PMI will show whether the post-holiday restart is lifting activity.
Credit Impulse

The credit pulse is being pushed from the top. Al Jazeera reported the PBOC governor vowing support amid 'weak links' [[n0222]], and Bloomberg reported the PBOC pumping in more liquidity, spurring gains in Chinese stocks [[n0198]]. That follows January's cuts to key lending rates — one for the first time in nearly two years, per CNBC [[n0164]] — and to medium-term and reverse-repo rates, per Fibre2Fashion [[n0167]]. Bloomberg described China's central bank seizing the moment for stimulus as the Fed hikes [[n0169]]. The constraint is local-government leverage: the SCMP reported banks being told to support rural infrastructure without adding to hidden debt [[n0187]]. The impulse should turn up, but it is being rationed toward infrastructure rather than used to reflate property.
Property

Property remains the policy test. The Khmer Times reported China excluding affordable rental housing from property credit controls [[n0220]] — targeted relief, not a broad bailout. Corporate stress is still surfacing: Bloomberg, citing Caixin, reported China's Cedar unable to pay $3.1 billion overdue [[n0188]], a reminder that credit stress is not confined to property developers. Onshore investors are reading these as idiosyncratic for now; the Shanghai Composite's +0.80% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18) says they expect credit carve-outs to widen. A stabilisation in home sales would confirm that view; a missed payment from a larger name would break it.
Fiscal, Policy & Trade

Policy is simultaneously supportive and punitive. The WSJ reported China ordering cuts to food-delivery fees, sparking a tech selloff [[n0847]], and Bloomberg said the policy wiped $26 billion off Meituan's value [[n0848]] — common prosperity is now a margin story, not only an antitrust one. Trade friction is rising on two fronts: Reuters reported the US adding e-commerce sites operated by Tencent and Alibaba to its 'notorious markets' list [[n0259]], the BBC reported Washington accusing China of 'serious harm' to workers through trade [[n0236]], and Reuters reported the EU imposing anti-dumping tariffs on Chinese steel fasteners [[n0243]]. On Russia, the SCMP reported Beijing warning that Western sanctions will worsen the Ukraine crisis [[n1351]], which could leave Chinese banks and exporters exposed if sanctions widen.
Markets & Flows

The tape shows the split cleanly. KWEB fell -5.04% on the session and Alibaba's US ADR -4.37%, while the CSI 300 tracker ASHR rose +2.22% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). Tencent in Hong Kong fell -1.88% to 446.40 HKD yet is still +6.94% over 20 sessions, and Business Insider reported Tencent joining the world's ten most valuable companies as Meta slid [[n0716]]. Allocators are rotating rather than exiting: Caixin reported Hillhouse buying NEV makers while ditching Alibaba and Bilibili [[n0480]], and CNBC reported banks from Credit Suisse to Goldman Sachs saying it is time to buy Chinese stocks [[n0207]]. Lenovo announced its selection as a Hang Seng Index constituent [[n0915]], which should add passive demand for hardware over platforms.
New / Most Important

The food-delivery fee order is the most important signal because it shows Beijing still willing to regulate margins directly even while the PBOC eases. Offshore platforms fell into the weekend, and Pinduoduo -6.05%, Baidu -5.22% and JD.com -3.61% on the session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18) show investors applying the same template across the sector. NPR reported the Beijing Winter Games coming to a close [[n0269]], which removes one reason for policy calm. The next loan prime rate fixing is the test of whether January's cuts extend.
Playbook ✓

Action: own onshore beta through ASHR against an underweight in offshore platforms through KWEB, sized as a pair. Trigger: a loan prime rate or reserve-ratio cut, or wider property credit carve-outs, to add to the long leg; another fee or data directive to add to the short. What changes the call: a Russia-sanctions spillover into Chinese banks or a broad Hong Kong lockdown would hit both legs, so the pair stays small. ⚠ Divergence: over 20 sessions the Hang Seng is +0.89% while the Shanghai Composite is -0.87% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18) — offshore had been outperforming until the latest five sessions, and Tencent's 20-session gain says part of the platform discount may already be priced.

geo.label: Dovish BOJ, import-cost squeeze
parts: Macro Stance

Japan's recovery is real but fragile. Reuters reported the economy rebounding on solid spending before Omicron clouded the outlook [[n1462]], while Al Jazeera reported exports growing less than expected as the trade deficit soared [[n1480]]. The Nikkei 225 closed at 27,122.07 index points, -0.41% on the session and -2.07% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). Mixed: domestic reopening is supportive, but an energy-driven terms-of-trade loss and chip shortages cap earnings.
Activity & Currency

The external account is the pressure point. The Seattle Times reported Japan's imports hitting record highs on surging energy prices [[n1443]], and with Brent at 93.54 USD/bbl (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18) the import bill keeps widening the kind of deficit that tends to weigh on the yen. Policy is the other half: the BOJ is still pushing negative rates through the system — Asahi reported it applying the minus rate to MUFG Bank deposits [[n1449]] — but Reuters said a board reshuffle may open scope for a less dovish BOJ [[n1470]]. Industry is supply-constrained: Automotive Logistics reported Toyota cutting March production plans because of the chip shortage [[n1787]], and Toyota Motor is -6.77% over 20 sessions at 2,184.00 JPY. Asahi's report that TSMC will expand its new Japan chip factory with Denso taking a stake [[n1473]] is the medium-term offset.
Playbook ✓

Action: prefer domestic reopening exposure over exporters and chip-equipment names, where the de-rating has been sharpest — Sony Group is -6.07% over five sessions and Tokyo Electron -7.34% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). Trigger: a hawkish signal from the reshaped BOJ board would favour banks, and easing chip supply would reopen the exporter trade. What changes the call: Brent holding above 93.54 USD/bbl deepens the trade deficit and the squeeze on household real incomes.

geo.label: RBA patience under pressure
parts: Macro Stance

Australia combines hot domestic data with a central bank that refuses to copy the Fed. The WSJ reported the Australian central bank won't follow the Fed on rate increases [[n0064]], even after the AFR's 3.5 per cent inflation shock [[n0009]] and The Australian's report of a 13-year-low jobless rate [[n0004]]. The S&P/ASX 200 closed at 7,221.70 index points, -1.02% on the session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). Mixed.
Demand & Financing

Demand is resilient but squeezed: the ABC reported record petrol prices that may be hurting wallets in more ways than one [[n0030]], Roy Morgan put January inflation expectations at 4.9% [[n0071]], and The Age reported NAB finding 1 in 5 Australians quit their job last year [[n0073]] — a tight labour market that supports wage pass-through. Corporate reporting splits by exposure: Reuters said Wesfarmers' profit dipped after a 'perfect pandemic storm' [[n0627]], while BHP's first-half profit beat estimates [[n0290]]. Iron ore is the risk: Reuters reported China urging some traders to cut inventory [[n0056]], and Fortescue Metals fell -13.05% over five sessions to 19.85 AUD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). Australian Broker News reported CBA forecasting when rates will rise [[n0069]] — the market is already ahead of the RBA.
Playbook ✓

Action: favour banks and domestic retail over iron-ore miners. Trigger: Beijing easing its pressure on iron-ore inventories would reopen the miners, while a hawkish RBA shift would support Commonwealth Bank at 97.75 AUD. What changes the call: a Chinese property relapse would hit both the miners and the banks through the terms of trade.

geo.label: NBP tightening on the front line
parts: Macro Stance

Poland is where the inflation shock and the security shock meet. Forsal.pl, citing GUS, reported January inflation at 9.2% [[n1597]], and the SII investor association noted it stayed below 10% but is still the highest this century [[n1599]]. The Monetary Policy Council has already lifted rates to the highest in almost nine years, per Rzeczpospolita [[n1548]], and TheBanker.com reported NBP governor Glapiński taking aim at inflation [[n1519]]. Growth is holding up — TVN24 reported GDP moving higher [[n1536]], Newseria described services as out of breath while production catches a second wind [[n1608]], and pb.pl reported the average wage rising 9.6% in 2021 [[n1551]] — so the NBP has room to keep going. But DW reported Belarus, Poland's eastern neighbour, continuing military drills with Russia [[n1426]]. Bearish: real-rate repair and a geopolitical risk premium are competing for the same asset prices.
Markets

Polish assets are trading as a frontline proxy. The Beta ETF WIG20TR tracker closed at 37.00 PLN, -2.48% over five sessions and -5.61% over 20 sessions, and the US-listed EPOL fell -4.93% over 20 sessions to 20.24 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). Bankier.pl reported the złoty recovering losses while the Ukraine question hit markets [[n1579]] — the currency is behaving like a risk barometer. Money.pl reported gold rising and Ukrainian companies falling on the conflict [[n1655]], and Parkiet examined how markets would react if a global armed conflict broke out [[n1632]]. Banks carry much of the beta: mBank fell -3.53% on the session to 453.40 PLN, and PKO Bank Polski is -3.95% over five sessions at 45.77 PLN. Fitch's rating decision, which Money.pl said flagged high inflation and problems with the European Commission [[n1692]], ties the sovereign story to Brussels as well as Moscow.
Fiscal & Politics

The fiscal debate has moved from tax design to debt service. Money.pl argued public debt will rise because of the NBP and become increasingly costly over time [[n1690]], and Business Insider Polska carried an expert explaining how rate rises lift the cost of public debt [[n1697]], even as Rzeczpospolita noted inflation is helping the government manage its debt [[n1547]]. Polski Ład remains politically toxic: Interia reported a poll on whether it hurt Law and Justice [[n1569]], Next Gazeta reported President Duda wanting comprehensive changes — a possible Polski Ład 2.0 [[n1620]] — and Interia reported another senior departure from the finance ministry [[n1565]]. Brussels is the swing factor: Rzeczpospolita reported the CJEU confirming 'euro for rule of law' as Ziobro attacked Morawiecki [[n1642]], the BBC reported Poland and Hungary losing their EU funding fight [[n1507]], and EUobserver reported Warsaw saying it is edging toward a rule-of-law deal [[n1524]].
Corporate & Sectors

Stock-level dispersion is wide. StockWatch.pl reported Allegro at new lows [[n1683]]; the e-commerce platform is -16.28% over 20 sessions at 32.65 PLN (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18), the local echo of the global de-rating of pandemic winners. Dino Polska is -16.45% over 20 sessions while DlaHandlu.pl reported Aldi, Biedronka, Dino and Lidl hiring almost 2,300 people [[n1637]] — labour costs are rising across food retail. CD Projekt released its next-generation Cyberpunk 2077 update and free trial, per its investor relations page [[n1585]], yet the stock is -6.02% over 20 sessions, and Antyweb reported The Witcher 3's director leaving to found Rebel Wolves [[n1639]]. Commodities offer the offset: coking-coal producer JSW is +15.19% over 20 sessions, and KGHM, +5.95%, is pushing small modular reactors in Poland by 2029, per eKoszalin [[n1604]]. Utilities lag: PGE is -5.60% over five sessions as Super Express reported it selling the Przeworsk CHP plant for a fraction of its former price [[n1628]].
Geopolitics & Security

Poland's security posture is hardening fast. Reuters reported the US announcing Abrams tanks for Poland as the Russia threat mounts [[n1525]], The National Interest reported additional US F-15s sent to bolster NATO's eastern flank [[n1517]], and the American Homefront Project reported Fort Bragg's 82nd Airborne deploying to Poland [[n1494]]. CNBC reported US troops preparing to help refugees if Russia invades [[n1492]]. Diplomacy is strained: TVN24 quoted Foreign Minister Rau, after talks with Lavrov, saying European security is in deep crisis [[n1613]], and Interia reported Maria Zakharova accusing the Polish government of acting in US rather than Polish interests [[n1656]]. Notes From Poland reported a UK–Poland–Ukraine trilateral agreement 'in face of Russian aggression' [[n1521]], while the Guardian reported Belarus saying Russian troops will remain indefinitely [[n1437]]. Energy security is the economic channel: Biznes Alert quoted Woźniak rejecting any new Yamal contract with the Russians [[n1577]].
New / Most Important

The new information is the convergence of three costs. Inflation above 9%, as Bankier.pl reported [[n1600]], forces the NBP to keep hiking; the debt bill rises with every hike; and the weekend's escalation lifts the risk premium on everything priced in złoty. Energy is the hidden accelerator: the energy regulator URE reported a record price for gas imported from EU countries in the fourth quarter of 2021 [[n1571]], Money.pl reported firms switching en masse to consumer gas tariffs [[n1698]], and IntelliNews noted Central Europe remains tied to Russia's pipeline network [[n1502]]. Bankier.pl reported apartment owners 'rubbing their hands' at the prospect of conflict-driven demand [[n1682]], a reminder that an inflow from Ukraine could add to housing inflation.
Playbook ✓

Action: stay underweight Polish equities against core Europe through the WIG20TR tracker and EPOL, preferring coal and copper exposure over banks and e-commerce. Trigger: tangible de-escalation plus a rule-of-law deal with Brussels would justify closing the underweight; a break below the tracker's 37.00 PLN close after an escalation would justify adding. What changes the call: a CPI peak that lets the NBP pause. ⚠ Divergence: rate hikes should lift Polish banks' margins, yet mBank, PKO Bank Polski and Bank Pekao are down -4.63%, -3.95% and -3.76% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18) — the geopolitical discount is overwhelming the earnings upgrade, and Analizy.pl reported average deposit rates rising clearly in December [[n1675]], which narrows part of that margin gain.
Narrative

Technology is splitting by cash generation. XLK closed at 152.44 USD, -1.01% on the session and -1.58% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18), as bear-flattening rates weigh on duration while some companies are still raising guidance.
Reported

Reuters reported Cisco raising its annual earnings forecast and announcing $15 billion in buybacks [[n1090]], and CNBC's Investing Club called it a beat and raise that defied the doubters [[n1102]]; Cisco Systems is +6.14% over five sessions at 57.21 USD. Shopify, by contrast, closed down 16% after warning that the pandemic boost will fade, per CNBC [[n0640]].
EPS Upside Watch

Networking hardware with pricing power — Cisco and Arista Networks, +4.13% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18) — is where estimates can still rise. Reuters' report that Palantir's margins will take a hit from higher spending in its commercial push [[n0785]] marks the opposite end: high-spend software where margins are under pressure.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Tom's Hardware reported AMD's market capitalisation surpassing Intel's for the first time [[n0381]]. The old hardware hierarchy is no longer a safe default; incumbency now trades at a discount until execution proves otherwise.
Narrative

Communication services sit at the epicentre of the ad-model reset. XLC closed at 67.41 USD, -6.66% over 20 sessions, and Meta Platforms (FB) is -32.00% over the same span at 206.16 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). Bloomberg reported Meta losing its top-10 ranking by market value amid its worst month ever [[n0773]].
Reported

Reuters reported Roku's revenue missing on supply-chain snags as the shares fell 20% [[n0793]], and Deadline reported ViacomCBS shares tumbling nearly 20% the day after its Paramount rebrand and streaming outlook [[n0658]]. Margin-diluting costs, from supply snags to streaming spend, are being punished.
EPS Upside Watch

The WSJ's account of Facebook's $10 billion breakup with advertisers [[n1155]] and the Guardian's report that Google will limit personal information shared on Android [[n0596]] point to a tougher tracking regime. The upside is narrow: Netflix rose +1.19% on the session and Snap is +18.34% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18), so distinctive engagement still earns a premium.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Reuters reported Trump's Truth Social app set for release in Apple's App Store, per an executive [[n0932]]. Digital World Acquisition (DWAC), +15.32% over 20 sessions at 84.32 USD, is a social-media bet priced on a launch rather than on advertising economics.
Narrative

Financials should be rate beneficiaries, but the flattening curve and a geopolitical hit to capital markets cap the upside. XLF closed at 39.22 USD, -2.22% over five sessions but +2.67% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18); JPMorgan Chase is +4.87% over 20 sessions while Morgan Stanley is -8.75% over five.
Reported

Reuters reported AIG's profit beating estimates on general insurance strength [[n1088]], and Bank of America's CEO saying capital-markets business is down but pipelines are full [[n0704]]. Reuters reported Goldman Sachs lifting its targets to win over skeptics [[n0745]], while the FT saw new targets but the same existential angst [[n0746]].
EPS Upside Watch

Net interest income is the cleanest upside as the 2Y reprices, and regional banks via KRE, +2.70% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18), are more leveraged to it than trading-heavy firms. The WSJ's report that regulators are probing block trading at Morgan Stanley, Goldman and other Wall Street firms [[n0322]] is a headline risk for the latter.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Yahoo Finance reported Buffett investing $1B in Bitcoin-friendly Nubank [[n0525]]: the most conservative allocator in finance is buying a digital bank, while European lenders such as Societe Generale are -10.01% over five sessions as the Russia standoff escalated.
Narrative

Energy is the market's war hedge and inflation hedge at once. XLE closed at 68.05 USD, +8.97% over 20 sessions, with Brent at 93.54 USD/bbl and WTI at 91.07 USD/bbl (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). Reuters reported oil hitting seven-year highs as the market feared an imminent Russian attack [[n0093]].
Reported

Supply remains tight: Reuters said an IEA demand revision confirmed a tighter oil market [[n0364]], and Middle East Eye reported Saudi Arabia rejecting a US request to raise production [[n1266]]. Offshore Engineer reported Tenaris expecting further sales and margin gains in the first half [[n1143]], and Reuters reported Norway's oil firms lifting their 2022 investment plans [[n0780]].
EPS Upside Watch

Occidental Petroleum, +17.21% over 20 sessions, and Schlumberger, +10.59% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18), reward operating leverage to price and to the capex cycle. Exxon Mobil at 77.36 USD has lagged that move, which leaves room for upward estimate revisions if crude holds near current levels.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The bear case is diplomatic, not economic: Reuters reported the US in the 'very final stages' of Iran nuclear talks [[n1375]] and Asian refiners eager to resume Iranian oil imports [[n1845]]. A Vienna deal could shave the risk premium even if Russia escalates.
Narrative

Industrials are caught between pricing power and cost inflation. XLI closed at 98.34 USD, -2.83% over 20 sessions, and Caterpillar is -10.34% over the same span (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18), as investors discount a slower cycle.
Reported

Reuters reported Deere aiming for a bigger profit as price hikes powered an earnings beat [[n0852]], yet Deere fell -3.00% on the session. AirGuide reported Airbus posting a record $4.8 billion net income and pulling away from Boeing [[n1844]], while Reuters reported Schindler warning on profit and China after a fall in fourth-quarter earnings [[n0232]].
EPS Upside Watch

Defence is where estimates have support: Raytheon Technologies (RTX) is +7.06% over 20 sessions and General Dynamics +4.49% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18), and DW reported the US set to sell Abrams tanks to Poland [[n1526]]. On costs, FreightWaves reported freight rate hikes over the past two years were unprecedented [[n1874]], which keeps pressure on margins for transport-intensive manufacturers.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Reuters reported the US will inspect new 787 Dreamliners because Boeing cannot self-certify [[n0517]], and that American Airlines plans more schedule cuts while it waits for 787 deliveries [[n0837]]. Regulatory friction, not demand, is now Boeing's binding constraint.
Narrative
Consumer discretionary is flat over 20 sessions, with XLY at 180.00 USD, -0.23% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18), but that hides violent dispersion: Amazon is +6.98% while Tesla is -9.21%.
Reported

Reuters reported DoorDash shares soaring 24% on a revenue beat [[n0575]], and CNBC reported Airbnb beating with strong guidance [[n0385]]; yet DoorDash fell -8.40% and Airbnb -4.74% on the session. Bloomberg reported Kering shares surging as Gucci sales rebounded [[n0763]], while Reuters said production caps curbed growth at Hermès [[n0884]].
EPS Upside Watch

Price is the lever: Reuters reported Louis Vuitton set to raise price tags as costs climb [[n0461]], and Supply Chain Dive reported Starbucks accelerating price increases to offset Omicron costs [[n1047]]. The margin risk shows in Business Insider's report that Shake Shack is delaying openings because of soaring construction costs and a lack of labour [[n0892]].
⚡ Breaking Convention

Reuters reported the US investigating 416,000 Tesla vehicles over unexpected braking reports [[n1867]]; for the sector's largest growth weight, regulatory risk now matters as much as demand. DraftKings fell -21.62% on the session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18), and Yahoo Finance's explanation of why sports betting is a low-margin business [[n1119]] shows why any wobble in the path to profit is punished.
Narrative

Staples are the cleanest expression of pricing power in an inflationary, risk-off tape. XLP closed at 76.03 USD, +1.04% over five sessions while the S&P 500 fell -1.58% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18); Coca-Cola is +3.73% and Procter & Gamble +2.31% over five sessions.
Reported

The New York Times reported Walmart's profits growing as consumers kept spending [[n0817]], and ET Retail reported Kraft Heinz beating on raised prices and robust demand [[n0766]]. Reuters said Nestlé is confident cost inflation won't take a bite out of margins [[n0775]], and CNBC reported Coca-Cola beating as demand for drinks away from home topped pre-pandemic levels [[n1017]].
EPS Upside Watch

Modern Retail reported Walmart gaining grocery market share thanks to continued inflation [[n0815]] — scale retailers can push price while trading customers down. The watch item is volume: CNBC reported Walmart saying shoppers are on alert as grocery bills climb [[n0818]].
⚡ Breaking Convention

Bloomberg argued Walmart has a cart full of reasons to love inflation [[n0814]], inverting the textbook: in this cycle the defensive sector is also an inflation beneficiary. The counterweight is retailer pushback — Reuters reported European retailers driving hard bargains with food giants [[n0742]].
Narrative

Health care is defensive in name but split in practice. XLV closed at 127.51 USD, -2.10% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18), as the COVID franchise unwinds: Moderna is -9.66% over five sessions and Pfizer -8.07% over 20, while AbbVie is +9.13% over 20.
Reported

CNBC reported Moderna's CEO saying it is reasonable to think the pandemic may be in its final stages [[n0608]], and Reuters reported Moderna eyeing a COVID booster by August without clarity on whether an Omicron-specific shot is needed [[n0610]]. Fierce Pharma reported Bayer raising Nubeqa's peak sales estimate to more than €3B [[n1128]].
EPS Upside Watch

Pipelines over pandemics: Fierce Pharma reported Bristol Myers scoring an FDA priority review in its expansion bid for Breyanzi [[n1129]], while STAT asked whether newly public biotechs trading below cash is as bad as it looks [[n1733]]. XBI is -4.24% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18), so selectivity matters more than sector beta.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Reuters reported Moderna developing an mRNA-based shingles vaccine [[n0880]]. The market is being asked to value the platform rather than the pandemic, and until those programmes carry revenue the vaccine makers trade like cyclicals, not defensives.
Narrative

Materials are where Russia risk becomes a supply premium. Alcoa is +39.12% over 20 sessions at 78.20 USD, aluminum futures are +9.20% at 3,304.50 USD/t and palladium +11.19% at 2,335.40 USD/oz (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18), even as XLB itself is flat at 83.86 USD.
Reported

Reuters reported Glencore setting aside $1.5 billion for probes while posting record earnings [[n1063]], and Reuters reported DuPont shedding its mobility and materials unit in an $11 billion Celanese deal [[n0858]]. Barron's argued DuPont stock is a buy as CEO Ed Breen works his magic [[n0856]].
EPS Upside Watch

Reuters' warning that commodity supplies are at risk if Russia is hit by sanctions [[n0850]] is the upside case for aluminium, palladium and fertiliser producers; CF Industries is +11.02% and Mosaic +14.47% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18).
⚡ Breaking Convention

The Financial Post reported Barrick's CEO suggesting miners are overpaying for assets amid higher gold prices [[n0705]] — a producer warning against its own sector's capital allocation, worth heeding with gold at 1,899.80 USD/oz.
Narrative

Real estate is the sector priced most directly off the 10Y. XLRE closed at 44.68 USD, -4.71% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18), and the Orange County Register put mortgage rates at 3.92%, the highest in 33 months [[n2013]].
Reported

Reuters reported US existing home sales accelerating as investors elbowed out first-time buyers [[n2025]], and the Real Economy Blog reported housing permits reaching a 15-year high [[n2004]]: demand is intact even as financing costs rise.
EPS Upside Watch

The Real Deal reported Blackstone buying a multifamily REIT in a $5.8B deal [[n0560]], and the WSJ reported Blackstone's European last-mile logistics deal valuing Mileway at $24 billion [[n0437]]. Rental and logistics cash flows are being bid in private markets even as listed property de-rates.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Private capital is arbitraging the public discount: Bloomberg reported Wall Street buying starter homes to quietly become America's landlord [[n0262]]. Public REITs fall with rates while private buyers pay up for the same assets — take-privates, not earnings beats, are the sector's re-rating mechanism.
Narrative

Utilities have failed as a haven. XLU closed at 66.22 USD, -1.21% over five sessions and -3.81% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18), even through a risk-off week, because the rate channel is overpowering the defensive bid; NextEra Energy is -10.23% over 20 sessions.
Reported

CNBC reported Southern Company's CEO saying hybrid work is driving residential energy demand [[n0754]], but WABE reported Georgia Power's $30B nuclear plant delayed by up to six more months [[n0676]]; Southern Company is -4.52% over five sessions.
EPS Upside Watch

Coal retirement is a rate-base story: POWER Magazine reported Duke Energy eyeing a coal phaseout by 2035 [[n0729]], and Duke rose +1.09% on the session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). Regulated capex supports earnings growth, but at a higher discount rate.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Europe shows the policy risk: Reuters reported EDF getting $2 bln of state help over nuclear-plant outages [[n0860]]. When power prices spike, governments step into utility economics, so the inflation hedge can become a political target.
Narrative

European autos sit at the intersection of chip supply and Russia risk. The iShares SXAP tracker closed at 61.27 EUR, -1.64% over five sessions and -2.81% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18), with Volkswagen preference shares -4.53% over five sessions at 180.10 EUR.
Reported

Reuters reported Volkswagen expecting the chip shortage to ease later in 2022 [[n0663]] and, citing Manager Magazin, VW in talks with Huawei on an autonomous driving unit [[n0813]]. Obserwator Gospodarczy reported German car production still falling, 40% below its level of three years ago [[n1552]].
EPS Upside Watch

Mercedes-Benz Group, +5.09% over 20 sessions at 75.59 EUR, and Renault, +9.03% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18), show pricing and mix carrying earnings while volumes are constrained. Reuters reported Stellantis' Maserati unveiling its new Grecale luxury SUV on March 22 [[n0506]], a product catalyst for the group.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Fortune argued the chip shortage that crippled parts of the world economy would get even worse with a Russian invasion of Ukraine [[n1785]]. The healing supply chain becomes the transmission channel for war risk, so the 'shortage easing' trade and the 'Russia risk' trade cannot both be right.
Narrative

Semiconductors are holding up better than the wider growth complex: SOXX closed at 466.57 USD, +0.55% over five sessions and -1.28% over 20, and the PHLX Semiconductor Index at 3,384.30 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). ASML's US line is +3.12% over five sessions while TSMC's ADR is -1.40%.
Reported

NVIDIA announced its fourth-quarter and fiscal 2022 results [[n0114]], and Al Jazeera reported the chipmaker forecasting upbeat current-quarter revenue [[n1821]]; Nvidia still fell -3.53% on the session. Reuters reported AMD closing its record purchase of Xilinx for an estimated $50 billion [[n0286]].
EPS Upside Watch

Memory and equipment carry the upside: Micron Technology is +10.83% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18), and Asahi reported TSMC expanding its new Japan factory with Denso taking a stake [[n1473]]. The laggard is Intel, whose plan SemiAnalysis described as 'throwing the kitchen sink' [[n1877]]; Intel fell -5.32% on the session.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Techcircle reported the FTC saying the termination of Nvidia's attempted Arm acquisition bodes well for competition [[n1833]], and Reuters reported Taiwan boosting protection for its semiconductor secrets [[n0644]]. Chip strategy is now industrial policy, and national-security rules — not only cycles — will set the sector's multiples.

earnings_pattern.title: Pricing power paid, pandemic pull-forward punished
parts: Rewarded

The market is paying for proven pricing and unit growth. CNBC reported DoorDash shares soaring after record order numbers [[n0726]], the AFR reported Treasury Wine shares surging as it lifts some luxury-brand prices [[n0234]], and the AFR also reported JB Hi-Fi shares jumping on a capital return and sales lift [[n1037]]. CNBC's Investing Club framed Cisco's quarter as a beat and raise that defied the doubters [[n1102]], and RSU by PriceLabs' review of Airbnb's fourth-quarter results [[n1150]] described great earnings, with questions lingering only over supply growth.
Punished

Growth normalisation is punished hard. CNBC reported Roblox closing down 26% after an earnings miss [[n0634]], Al Jazeera reported Shopify plunging 17% on a weaker growth outlook [[n1830]], and Reuters reported Paramount shares slumping as investments to beef up streaming spooked investors [[n0623]]. Reuters said pandemic-era darling Delivery Hero was punished as earnings disappointed [[n1020]], and Bloomberg reported Sea's $16 billion crash signalling trouble beyond its India shutout [[n0494]].
Pattern

Three rules are working. First, guidance beats the quarter: CNBC reported Shopify closing lower after warning that the pandemic boost will fade [[n0640]], even though the business is still growing. Second, price beats volume: Food Manufacturing reported Kraft Heinz scoring big profits in 2021 even as its fourth quarter showed challenges [[n0765]], and Deere's beat rested on price hikes [[n0852]]. Third, in a risk-off tape even winners give back gains — DoorDash fell -8.40% and Deere -3.00% on the session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18), so post-earnings drift turns negative unless the macro backdrop clears.
Attention into EPS

Attention has shifted from users to monetisation. Mobilegamer.biz reported Roblox nearing 55m DAUs with Q4 revenues up 83% [[n1139]], yet Game Developer reported its slowing growth starting to worry investors [[n1164]] — bookings, not engagement, set the price. The same lens will be applied to the next retail and software prints: margin commentary and pricing will matter more than top-line beats.
Playbook

Action: buy beats that come with raised guidance or explicit pricing power, and fade post-print rallies in pandemic beneficiaries. Trigger: a guidance raise followed by a positive session in a falling tape. What changes the call: a geopolitical de-escalation rally would lift the punished growth names indiscriminately, so the fade should be hedged against a sharp short-covering bounce.

underowned.title: Aluminium and platinum-group metals: the sanctions supply premium
parts: Attention Gap

Equity attention is fixed on crude and gold, but Alcoa is +39.12% over 20 sessions at 78.20 USD against +8.97% for XLE, while platinum is +5.70% over five sessions at 1,075.30 USD/oz (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18).
Exposure & Risk

Reuters warned commodity supplies are at risk if Russia is hit by sanctions [[n0850]], and the Guardian's list of London-listed Russian firms that could be hit [[n0901]] underlines how close metals supply sits to the sanctions perimeter. Exposure runs through Alcoa, aluminum futures and palladium; the risk is that de-escalation removes the premium quickly while soft Chinese demand caps the base case.
Trigger to Watch

Formal Western sanctions naming Russian metals producers would extend the move; tangible diplomatic progress would compress it. Watch whether aluminum holds its 3,304.50 USD/t level when trading resumes after the US holiday.

underowned.title: China A-shares: the easing trade behind the platform noise
parts: Attention Gap

Global investors are fixated on Beijing's platform crackdown, but onshore equities are trading the PBOC instead: ASHR is up over five sessions and closed at 36.82 USD, and the Shanghai Composite rose +0.66% on the session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18).
Exposure & Risk

The BBC reported China cutting interest rates as economic growth slowed [[n0157]], and CNBC reported investment banks from Credit Suisse to Goldman Sachs calling time to buy Chinese stocks [[n0207]]; with KWEB -2.55% over the same five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18), the call is working onshore first. Exposure: ASHR and large-cap onshore financials and industrials. Risk: corporate credit events, an Omicron spread from Hong Kong into the mainland, or secondary sanctions tied to Russia.
Trigger to Watch
A further loan prime rate or reserve-ratio cut, or wider property-credit carve-outs, would confirm the trade; a new regulatory directive aimed at onshore sectors would undermine it.

underowned.title: US gas exporters: Europe's insurance policy
parts: Attention Gap

While Europe's TTF price has eased, US Henry Hub gas is +12.43% over five sessions at 4.43 USD/MMBtu (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18) — the US side of the transatlantic gas trade is repricing first.
Exposure & Risk

Brookings argued now is not the time to limit US natural gas exports [[n1275]], Texas Monthly described how Texas is rescuing Europe from the Russians [[n1217]], and the EIA forecast US marketed gas production rising in 2022 and 2023 [[n1868]]. Exposure runs through Henry Hub futures and producers such as ConocoPhillips, at 89.63 USD after a -4.16% five-session pullback. Risk: export capacity is finite, so a European shortage lifts LNG margins more than US wellhead prices.
Trigger to Watch
A disruption of Russian flows during Europe's refill season would widen the transatlantic spread; a diplomatic breakthrough would narrow it.

underowned.title: Grains and fertiliser: the Black Sea breadbasket premium
parts: Attention Gap

Soybeans are +13.24% over 20 sessions at 1,601.50 US cents/bu and corn +6.17% at 654.25 US cents/bu, while wheat is only +2.18% at 797.00 US cents/bu (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18) — the market has priced South American dryness faster than Black Sea risk.
Exposure & Risk

Successful Farming reported a dry South American soybean crop looking to improve with rain [[n1813]], while Al Jazeera mapped Russia's and Ukraine's role in global wheat supply [[n1857]] and a Reuters commentary argued Ukraine's unmatched corn crop gains are encroaching on rival exporters [[n1847]]. Exposure: wheat and corn futures and Nutrien, +7.00% over 20 sessions. Risk: rain and de-escalation can deflate both premiums at once.
Trigger to Watch

MarketWatch's warning that the Russia–Ukraine crisis may make food-price inflation even worse [[n1810]] becomes the base case if Black Sea shipping is disrupted; watch wheat relative to its 797.00 US cents/bu close.

crypto.title: Bitcoin fails the haven test
parts: Market Context

Crypto is trading as high-beta risk, not digital gold. Bitcoin's last completed daily close was 38,431.38 USD, -4.21% on the day and -13.78% over five sessions, and Ether closed at 2,628.65 USD, -17.33% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2022-02-20). Gold, by contrast, gained +3.13% over five sessions to 1,899.80 USD/oz (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). Over 20 sessions Bitcoin is -0.13%, so the early-February rally has been given back as geopolitical fear rose. CNBC's outlook for bitcoin as geopolitical tensions heat up and interest rates rise [[n2045]] frames the dual pressure, and the listed proxies amplify it: Marathon Digital is -11.29% and Robinhood Markets -11.34% over five sessions.
New / Most Important

The structural news is constructive even as prices fall. Forbes reported Sequoia launching a $500 million fund to invest in crypto tokens [[n0990]], Ledger Insights reported stablecoin firm Circle doubling its valuation to $9 billion in a new SPAC deal [[n1304]], and Reuters reported Coinbase letting recipients in Mexico cash out in local currency [[n0956]]. Regulation is the counterweight: the Financial Stability Board warned of emerging risks from crypto-assets to global financial stability [[n0976]]. Bloomberg reported Ethereum founder Vitalik Buterin saying crypto 'welcomes' another winter [[n1001]] — an insider tone that matches the tape.
Playbook

Action: treat Bitcoin as a risk asset sized like a leveraged Nasdaq position rather than a war hedge, and use gold for the geopolitical tail. Trigger to re-engage: Bitcoin holding above 38,431.38 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2022-02-20) while equities stabilise, or a de-escalation that lifts the growth complex. What changes the call: a Bitcoin rally on an escalation headline would be the first real evidence of haven demand; without it, the miners and Coinbase Global — -2.76% over five sessions at 189.16 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18) — stay on the defensive.

flows.title: Liquidity tightens into a geopolitical shock
parts: Global Liquidity

Global liquidity is diverging by central bank. The Fed is about to start lifting rates, and Reuters' round-up of what global banks forecast for 2022 hikes [[n2078]] sits alongside its analysis of what could push the Fed to a 'Plan B' for balance-sheet reduction [[n1305]] — the market is planning for both higher rates and shrinking reserves. China is moving the other way, with the PBOC adding liquidity [[n0198]]. Europe sits in between: Reuters argued the ECB 'put' for euro-zone bond markets is some way off [[n1206]]. Further out, Reuters reported Eurodollar futures betting a hawkish Fed could ease slightly in 2024 [[n1272]], so the tightening window is seen as short. Bloomberg reported Treasury market liquidity eroding with the Fed's course a gamble [[n2057]]; thinner liquidity means geopolitical news moves prices more than usual, especially when US cash markets are closed for a holiday.
Rates & Dollar

Front-end repricing still dominates. With the 2Y at 1.47% and the 10Y at 1.92%, the 10Y-2Y spread stands at +45 bps after compressing 29 bps over 20 observations (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-18). Treasury ETFs show where the haven bid sits: TLT rose +1.05% on the session to 138.23 USD while SHY was flat at 84.47 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). The DXY is +0.42% over 20 sessions at 96.04 index points, and Reuters reported the dollar gaining as Ukraine worries rose and Bullard reiterated his rate comments [[n0087]]. A firmer dollar plus a flatter curve tightens conditions for emerging markets: EMB is -2.45% over 20 sessions at 103.00 USD.
Credit Check

Credit is weakening at the margin, not breaking. HYG is -2.98% over 20 sessions at 82.89 USD and LQD -4.05% at 123.68 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18): investment grade has lost more than high yield because duration, not default risk, is driving prices. Reuters reported global companies slowing debt-raising as yields climb [[n1292]], which eases supply pressure but signals rising funding costs, and Artemis reported insurance bonds showing resilience as spreads reset [[n1284]]. Asian stress is idiosyncratic but persistent: Bloomberg, citing Caixin, reported China's Cedar unable to pay $3.1 billion overdue [[n0188]]. Over five sessions HYG is +0.28% and LQD -0.93%, so credit has not joined equities in the geopolitical sell-off — a buffer that could close quickly if sanctions hit bank balance sheets in Europe.
Equity & Fund Flows

Positioning is lighter but not clean. Wolf Street reported margin debt plunging as stocks tumbled and high-fliers were crushed, though leverage is still gigantic [[n1310]], and Bloomberg reported a big options trade hedging an S&P 500 plunge of up to 20% by April [[n2043]]. STOXX reported VSTOXX futures seeing increased activity amid the pullback and ahead of French elections [[n1259]]. Long-only money is selective: CNBC reported Berkshire buying about $1 billion of Activision shares before Microsoft's deal [[n0300]], City AM reported Berkshire dumping Visa and Mastercard while buying Nubank [[n0665]], and Reuters reported California and Texas pension funds among new investors in Rivian [[n0402]]. Bloomberg reported Cathie Wood's ARKK still struggling a year from its peak [[n1720]]; ARKK is -9.87% over five sessions at 64.80 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18).
Portfolio Implication

With liquidity tightening and a binary geopolitical weekend, portfolios should be built to survive a gap rather than to maximise carry. Hold gold, +3.71% over 20 sessions at 1,899.80 USD/oz (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18), as the hedge that has worked; keep duration moderate because the 2Y still reprices with every Fed signal; and prefer short-dated high yield to long investment grade for carry. In equities, fund energy, staples and defence overweights from long-duration growth and Russia-sensitive European financials. The signal to re-risk is concrete diplomacy: the Guardian reported Macron paving the way for a potential Putin–Biden summit [[n1430]], and a confirmed meeting would argue for covering European and growth underweights first.

anticipatory.title: Invasion or summit: the weekend binary
parts: What Is Priced

Markets price a high but not certain probability of attack. The VIX at 27.75 index points sits below its 20-session reference of 28.85, gold is +3.13% over five sessions, and the S&P 500 is only -1.12% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). Axios reported Russia extending drills in Belarus, fuelling invasion fears [[n1435]], and Politico reported the build-up continuing despite Moscow's promises of a drawdown [[n1423]].
Conditional Expression

If Macron's effort to pave the way for a Putin–Biden summit, reported by the Guardian [[n1430]], produces a firm meeting, buy what has been punished — the Euro Stoxx 50, -3.67% over 20 sessions, and Russia-sensitive European banks — and trim gold. If the shelling that the Guardian reported raising tensions in east Ukraine [[n1395]] escalates into an attack, add energy, defence through ITA and gold, and short European banks.
Risk

The awkward middle is a limited move: steps on the separatist regions that trigger sanctions without full war, hurting Europe while leaving oil's premium unresolved. The Moscow Times reported the Kremlin holding all the cards as Russia-backed separatists demand recognition [[n1412]].

anticipatory.title: Fed lift-off: 25 or 50 basis points
parts: What Is Priced

The 2Y's +46 bps move over 20 observations to 1.47% (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-18) prices a March lift-off and a quick follow-up. Reuters reported the readout of the January meeting showing the Fed not wed to a particular pace of hikes [[n2066]], so the size of the first move is still open.
Conditional Expression

If Fed speakers validate Bullard's front-loading, extend the flattener — the 10Y-2Y at +45 bps still has room to compress — and stay underweight long-duration technology. If the Fed signals 25 bps and a measured path, as the New York Fed president's comments imply [[n2080]], the front end can rally and oversold growth stocks can bounce. The Philadelphia Fed's first-quarter Survey of Professional Forecasters [[n1972]] is the professional baseline against which either signal will be judged.
Risk

Geopolitics can short-circuit the Fed: an invasion that tightens financial conditions could make policymakers more cautious and steepen the curve from the front. Politico reported Republicans delaying the vote on Biden's Fed nominees [[n2056]], which adds governance noise to the reaction function.

anticipatory.title: Beijing's next move: easing versus regulation
parts: What Is Priced

ASHR's +2.22% over five sessions and KWEB's -5.04% on the session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18) price an easing PBOC alongside more platform regulation. Reuters reported China's inflation slowing, leaving room for policy easing [[n0205]], and the yuan slipping as US–China monetary policy diverges [[n0214]], so part of the easing is leaking into the currency.
Conditional Expression

If the next loan prime rate fixing or a reserve-ratio cut arrives, extend the long A-share leg. If regulators follow the food-delivery fee order — which the WSJ reported sparked a tech selloff [[n0847]] — with similar directives, add to the short KWEB leg. A pause in new rules would favour covering the short first, because Tencent's +6.94% over 20 sessions shows how sharply the platforms can rebound.
Risk

Hong Kong's Omicron wave is the shared risk: the WSJ reported hospital wards overflowing as Omicron defied zero-Covid policies [[n0208]]. Western sanctions on Russia that catch Chinese counterparties would also hit both legs at once.

anticipatory.title: Europe's gas refill and Nord Stream 2
parts: What Is Priced

Dutch TTF at 73.76 EUR/MWh, -6.61% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18), prices the winter as survived and little risk to the summer refill. Reuters' factbox on Russian gas pipeline exports to Europe [[n0794]] is a reminder of how much of the refill still depends on Russian flows.
Conditional Expression

If Russia keeps flows steady while talks continue — Reuters reported Putin saying Nord Stream 2 would cement Europe's energy security [[n1233]] — the refill trade favours European industrials with gas exposure. If flows are cut or sanctions target the pipeline, express it long US gas through Henry Hub-linked producers such as ConocoPhillips and short gas-intensive European industry.
Risk

Policy can cap both legs: Forbes reported France vowing to build more nuclear energy after being hit with high gas prices [[n1800]], and governments have shown a willingness to intervene in power markets. A mild spring would also ease the refill squeeze and the price.

catalysts.title: Cisco Systems (CSCO)
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Cisco raised its annual earnings forecast and announced $15 bln in share buybacks, per Reuters [[n1090]] — a rare combination of upgrade and capital return in a de-rating technology tape. Business Insider's list of companies Cisco could buy to beat rising competitors [[n1024]] adds strategic optionality.
Price Hurdle & Risk

Cisco Systems closed at 57.21 USD, +2.58% on the session and +6.14% over five sessions, but only +0.94% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18): the shares must hold the post-earnings gap. Risk: component shortages could delay shipments and turn backlog into deferred revenue.
Trade Expression
Buy pullbacks toward the pre-earnings range, funded by an underweight in high-multiple software; exit if the shares give back the full five-session gain.

catalysts.title: Intel (INTC)
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Fast Company described Pat Gelsinger's audacious $43.5B plan to revive Intel [[n0755]], and TechPowerUp reported Intel announcing a new Intel 18A node [[n1876]]. The ambition is real, but the spending profile is what investors are pricing, and Bloomberg reported Gelsinger is tired of Wall Street doubting his comeback plan [[n1101]].
Price Hurdle & Risk

Intel closed at 45.04 USD, -5.32% on the session and -13.45% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18), and Tom's Hardware reported AMD's market cap surpassing Intel's for the first time [[n0381]]. Until the spending shows returns, the stock lacks a floor. Risk to the bear case: the $5.4 billion Tower Semiconductor acquisition, announced by Intel [[n0454]], could revalue its foundry ambitions.
Trade Expression
Underweight Intel against AMD within semiconductors; cover if Intel reclaims its 20-session reference of 52.04 USD.

catalysts.title: Nvidia (NVDA)
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

AlphaStreet published a snapshot of Nvidia's fourth-quarter fiscal 2022 earnings [[n1133]], a print Barron's had framed as a big day for the metaverse after Roblox [[n0590]], and Al Jazeera reported an upbeat current-quarter revenue forecast [[n1821]]. Techcircle reported the FTC saying the end of the Arm acquisition attempt bodes well for competition [[n1833]], which removes a regulatory overhang but also a growth option.
Price Hurdle & Risk

Nvidia closed at 236.42 USD, -3.53% on the session and +1.15% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18): the beat has not lifted the stock out of its rate-driven range. Risk: higher real yields compress the multiple regardless of revenue momentum.
Trade Expression
Hold core exposure but add only if Nvidia outperforms SOXX after the holiday; cut if it breaks its 20-session reference of 233.74 USD.

catalysts.title: Walmart (WMT)
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Walmart is the clearest scale beneficiary of food inflation: the WSJ reported it withstanding pandemic blows and higher costs to boost business [[n1147]], and Al Jazeera reported it thriving despite supply-chain woes and high inflation [[n0816]]. Grocery share gains make price increases easier to pass through.
Price Hurdle & Risk

Walmart closed at 137.99 USD, +1.97% over five sessions but -1.57% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18); the hurdle is its 20-session reference of 140.19 USD. Risk: CNBC reported shoppers on alert as grocery bills climb [[n0818]], so trade-down could pressure margins if wage growth fades.
Trade Expression
Overweight Walmart against discretionary retail as the staples leg of the pricing-power trade; reassess if management commentary points to falling volumes.

catalysts.title: Alibaba (BABA)
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

The BBC reported Alibaba and Tencent sites added to the US 'Notorious Markets List' [[n0254]], and Barron's reported the same counterfeit and piracy designation [[n0253]], in the same week Bloomberg reported Beijing's new fee policy wiping $26 billion off Meituan's value [[n0848]]. Caixin reported Hillhouse ditching Alibaba while buying NEV makers [[n0480]].
Price Hurdle & Risk

Alibaba's US ADR closed at 118.99 USD, -4.37% on the session, and the Hong Kong line at 119.50 HKD, -2.85% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). The hurdle is the ADR's 20-session reference of 123.23 USD. Risk: a policy pivot pairing PBOC easing with regulatory relief could squeeze shorts.
Trade Expression
Hold BABA underweight as the short leg against ASHR; cover if the ADR reclaims 123.23 USD on a policy-easing signal.

catalysts.title: Airbus (AIR.PA)
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Statista reported Airbus soaring back out of the red [[n1843]], and AirGuide reported a record $4.8 billion net income pulling it away from Boeing [[n1844]]. Reuters reported Airbus finalising the sale of seven A350 freighters to Singapore Airlines [[n0387]], while US regulators are inspecting new Boeing 787s, per Reuters [[n0517]].
Price Hurdle & Risk

Airbus closed at 115.00 EUR, -2.95% over five sessions and +1.41% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). The WSJ reported its plan to ramp up production of its bestselling jet hitting snags [[n0695]], and Reuters reported Airbus reviewing its defence business as pressures mount [[n0578]]. Risk: the Seattle Times reported Airbus workers authorising a strike over pay at UK wing plants [[n1793]].
Trade Expression
Overweight Airbus against Boeing as the cleaner commercial-aerospace exposure; reassess if ramp snags force a cut to delivery targets.
